title: How to learn frontend (and keep improving)

plan.summary: How to learn frontend and keep improving: a repeatable read-build-measure-explain loop built on primary sources, browser-support literacy, and continuous practice.
outcomes: Explain the read-build-measure-explain loop and why it beats passive tutorials.
Decide whether a feature is safe to ship today using Baseline and caniuse.
Build a personal learning log that records each roadmap item's four steps.
Decide when to polyfill or progressively enhance instead of dropping support.
Explain how reading source code and teaching accelerate frontend expertise.

lesson_outline.title: Why a learning method matters
lesson_outline.visual_reason: A concrete failure story is enough for a developer to see why passive tutorials stall.

lesson_outline.title: The learning loop: read, build, measure, explain
lesson_outline.visual_reason: Four steps form one repeatable cycle; the end-to-end workflow view comes first.
lesson_outline.interaction_goal: Reorder the four steps and predict what breaks when a step is skipped.

lesson_outline.title: Primary sources over tutorials
lesson_outline.visual_reason: A static map of source types and their trust level is all this idea needs.
lesson_outline.interaction_goal: Match each source type to the trust it deserves.

lesson_outline.title: Know what you can ship: Baseline & caniuse
lesson_outline.visual_reason: Baseline labels map a feature to its ship-readiness, best drawn as a decision path.
lesson_outline.interaction_goal: Trace a feature through the Baseline labels and predict the ship decision.

lesson_outline.title: Feature detection, polyfills & progressive enhancement
lesson_outline.visual_reason: Three strategies differ by what the user gets when support is missing; a side-by-side view shows the trade-off.
lesson_outline.interaction_goal: Compare polyfill, progressive enhancement, and graceful degradation for one feature.

lesson_outline.title: Practice platforms & reading other people's code
lesson_outline.visual_reason: Reading a tiny library line by line teaches more than a summary; a walkthrough makes it concrete.
lesson_outline.interaction_goal: Step through a small library's source and predict what each branch returns.

lesson_outline.title: Teach in public & stay current
lesson_outline.visual_reason: A few recurring habits compound; a workflow diagram ties teaching, sharing, and staying current together.
lesson_outline.interaction_goal: Map each habit to the skill gap it closes.

mini_projects.use_case: A frontend team checks a list of CSS and JavaScript features against Baseline status and prints whether each is safe to ship today or needs a fallback.
A learner keeps one note per roadmap item with the read, build, measure, and explain steps, scaffolded by a small generator script.

capstone.name: Learning tracker
capstone.problem: A developer tracks their frontend learning: each roadmap item is a note with read, build, measure, and explain, and a dashboard shows progress and gaps.

learner.experience: software developer learning frontend end to end
goals: choose tools and approaches from evidence

curriculum.scope: Set up how a developer learns frontend and keeps improving: the learning loop, primary sources, browser-support literacy, and continuous practice.

discovery.note: Research proposed sub-concepts (release-notes-tracking, challenge-briefs, portfolio-and-review, ai-assisted-practice, writing-for-learners, review-feedback-loop) folded into their parents' coverage at standard depth; ecosystem-signals and open-source-etiquette deferred. findings.problem: Prose states a nanoid() call reads 21 secure random bytes and masks each to 6 bits; nanoid v3 customRandom computes step = 34 and reads 34 bytes, then uses 21 of them. The 21-characters/126-bits conclusion is correct; the byte count is not.
findings.fix: Reword to 'reads 34 secure random bytes (the step size) and masks 21 of them to 6-bit indices', or drop the byte count.

findings.problem: Card hlf-02 says 'versions older than 30 months do not' support a Newly available feature; the 30-month threshold marks Widely available, not which versions ship a feature.
findings.fix: Reword to 'browser versions released before the feature became Newly available lack it'.

findings.problem: frontendmentor-challenges is typed 'course' tier B, whose rubric requires a named instructor and a current syllabus; Frontend Mentor is a self-serve practice platform.
findings.fix: Strengthen why_trusted to justify the fit for a recognised practice platform.
